title: Baked Beef Salteñas with Juicy Spiced Stew Filling
summary: Hand-crimped pastry parcels filled with a juicy, spiced beef stew, egg and olives, baked until deep golden with a glossy, savoury filling inside.
equipment: 2 rimmed baking trays lined with baking paper

ingredients.item: stewing beef (chuck), cut into 1 cm dice
fine sea salt or table salt
medium onion, cut into 5 mm dice
cayenne pepper (or 1 tsp ají panca powder)
floury potato, peeled, in 1 cm dice
plain flour, plus extra for dusting
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Soak
steps.text: Sprinkle 10 g gelatine over 100 ml of the cold stock and leave for 5 min.

steps.title: Brown
steps.text: Season 600 g beef with ½ tsp salt and brown in the oil in 2 batches, 4-5 min each, then set aside.

steps.title: Soften
steps.text: Cook the onion and garlic in the same pan over medium until soft, 5 min, then stir in the cayenne, cumin, paprika, oregano and pepper for 1 min.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Return the beef with the remaining stock, 140 g potato, 90 g raisins and the remaining salt, bring to a simmer, cover and cook on low until the beef is tender, 50-60 min.

steps.title: Set
steps.text: Off the heat, stir in the soaked gelatine until dissolved, then 100 g peas, cool and chill until firm, at least 4 h or overnight.

steps.title: Dough
steps.text: Melt 225 g butter with the annatto, whisk 455 g flour, salt and sugar, pour in the butter and rub to a sandy texture, then add 175 ml hot water and mix to a smooth dough.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: Divide the dough into 9 pieces, roll each to a 20 cm round, fill with the cold stew, an egg quarter and 2 olive halves, then bring the edges up and crimp into a tall shape.

steps.title: Freeze
steps.text: Set the parcels on a tray and freeze for at least 4 h.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake the frozen parcels at 230 °C, brushed with egg white, until golden with dark crimp tips and the filling is piping hot, 20-25 min.

tips: Chilling the stew until it sets firm makes it much easier to parcel up without the filling leaking out.
Freezing the shaped parcels before baking helps the pastry hold its shape and keeps the filling from bursting through the seams.
Eat them standing up and bite the top off first, as the filling inside is deliberately juicy.
storage: Shaped, unbaked parcels can be kept frozen until needed; once baked, they are best eaten the same day while the pastry is crisp and the filling is piping hot. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
